I would answer: 1

As a parent, it's natural to be concerned about your child's well-being and want to understand what's going on. However, in this scenario, the therapist is bound by confidentiality laws and ethical guidelines that prohibit them from disclosing information about their clients, especially minors, without their consent.

By insisting that the therapist reveal why your son wants to see him, you are putting the therapist in a difficult position and potentially undermining the trust that your son has placed in them. This could damage the therapeutic relationship and make it more challenging for your son to open up and work through his issues.

It's essential to respect your son's autonomy and boundaries, especially as he's approaching adulthood. By not respecting his wish for confidentiality, you may be inadvertently creating more problems and straining your relationship with him.

It's not about whether you "deserve" to know or not; it's about respecting your son's right to privacy and confidentiality in his therapeutic relationship. Instead of insisting on knowing the details, you could try having an open and honest conversation with your son, letting him know that you're concerned and want to support him, but also respecting his boundaries and decisions.

In this case, the therapist's refusal to disclose information is not only legally and ethically sound but also in the best interest of your son's well-being and therapeutic progress.
